overall_summary: Analysis of 47 deduplicated Shorts reveals a sharp performance divide. The channel's primary growth engine is the 'What If You Fell Into...' extreme celestial survival format, along with mind-bending planetary physics (generating 800–1,050+ views and 15–38 likes per video, with strong recent velocity on uploads like Venus's orbital anomaly). In contrast, generic psychology facts, repeated identical uploads, and low-stakes trivia consistently stall under 100 views with near-zero engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: Immersive 'What If You Fell Into...' extreme cosmic hazard hooks
winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (823 views, 15 likes) dramatically outperform average channel benchmarks in both views and engagement.
winning_patterns.action: Produce high-stakes survival simulation Shorts placing the viewer directly into extreme cosmic phenomena, maintaining a tight 19–21s duration.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' reached 980 views and 21 likes within 8 days (~122.5 views/day), and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' hit 1,027 views and 36 likes.
winning_patterns.action: Spotlight scientifically verified, paradox-level cosmic mechanics that violate everyday intuition.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5–53 views across 3 uploads) and 'Songs Stuck In Your Head' (17–71 views) consistently floor out below 100 views.
weak_patterns.action: Deprecate routine human psychology and brain trivia unless framed as high-stakes mystery or sensory survival.

weak_patterns.evidence: Repeated titles like 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' (plummeted to 34 views on third upload) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' show diminishing returns.
weak_patterns.action: Enforce strict novelty checks; never recycle exact topics or scripts.
